pages.text: Sunlight filters through leaves as Fiona the forest hums with quiet life.
Tall trees stretch upward, their branches forming a leafy roof called the canopy.
Below the canopy, smaller plants grow. This layer stays cooler and shaded.
On the forest floor, leaves fall and break down. Soil becomes rich and dark.
Birds, insects, and animals move through each layer. Every level has its own helpers.
Trees breathe in a gas called carbon dioxide and release oxygen into the air.
Oxygen helps people and animals breathe. Forests help keep the air clean.
Forests grow in many places. Some are warm and wet, others are cool and quiet.
Fiona whispers: many living things depend on forests to survive.
At bedtime, we remember: forests have layers, clean the air, and shelter life.
